messages.subject: Glimmer source from github
parts:
For a little while, I've been using glimmer to host shiny apps. I wanted to have my apps update from github, so I copied an existing Shiny app from someone else to test if it would work. My copy of the app is here, my files look like: 

server.R:
eval(parse(text=RCurl::getURL("https://gist.github.com/jknowles/4484930/raw/server.R", ssl.verifypeer=FALSE)))

ui.R:
eval(parse(text=RCurl::getURL("https://gist.github.com/jknowles/4484930/raw/ui.R", ssl.verifypeer=FALSE)))

This seems to work fine, so what I'm wondering is, are there any drawbacks to this method?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: Glimmer source from github
parts: I guess the usual caution about eval-parse is in order. If someone hacks the gist and injects malicious code into the files, it could be a security issue.

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Glimmer source from github
parts:
I use a makefile to manage my Shiny apps, so that both the source on github and the app on glimmer are updated simultaneously. Here are the lines from my makefile. You need to  substitute username and repo with yours. When you do make deploy, the app will be pushed to github and to glimmer. Alternately, you could set up the rsync as a post-commit hook on your repo, but I prefer the control I get by using make.

deploy:
   git push g...@github.com:<username>/<repo>
   rsync -avz --delete <local-repo> <username>@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Glimmer source from github
parts:
That's a good solution. Another would be to clone the git repo (each gist is backed by a real git repo) directly in your glimmer ~/ShinyApps directory, then use this command whenever you want to make it update:

ssh <username>@glimmer.rstudio.com "cd ~/ShinyApps/<appdir> && git pull"
